Weber least-cost theory 1909: lowest total transport cost
MI > 1 near raw material; MI < 1 or ubiquitous inputs near market
Pure raw material (cotton) loses no weight, free to locate anywhere between source and market

new.s: In Weber's least-cost theory, a 'pure' raw material such as cotton, which loses no weight in processing, allows the industry to be located:
o: Anywhere between the source and the market
new.x: A pure raw material has no weight loss, so transport cost is the same whether raw material or product is moved; the plant is free to locate anywhere between source and market. Weight-losing inputs (MI > 1) pull it to the source (A); weight-gaining or ubiquitous inputs (MI < 1) pull it to the market (B); a port location (D) is not implied by the theory.
new.tq: Pure material (cotton) = free location; weight-losing = source; ubiquitous = market.
